summary: The right choice if content already flows through remark/rehype: it sanitizes the HAST tree against an explicit schema instead of round-tripping through the DOM. Zero advisories, tiny and type-safe, but no release since 2023 and a small community.
reasoning: Schema-based allowlist on the syntax tree, which avoids the HTML serialise/re-parse cycle where mXSS lives.
Two dependencies on hast-util-sanitize, 296 KB install, ESM with bundled types.
No advisories in OSV and no advisory history.
Fits the existing assistant-ui/react-markdown pipeline, which is already remark/rehype based.
The default schema is restrictive and safe; extending it is explicit.
caveats: Last release 2023 and only 224 stars. The engine, hast-util-sanitize, last shipped 5.0.2 in October 2024.
It only sanitizes HAST. It is not a function you can call on an HTML string.
Schema extensions are easy to get wrong: allowing style or className can reopen injection paths.
No provenance and no release automation.

evidence.label: Known advisories
evidence.detail: OSV returns no advisories for rehype-sanitize or its engine hast-util-sanitize.

evidence.label: Sanitization model
evidence.detail: Operates on HAST with an explicit schema; no HTML serialisation round-trip, so mXSS surface is smaller.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: 2 direct dependencies, 3 installed packages, 296 KB install, 20 KB unpacked.

evidence.label: Maintenance
evidence.detail: 6.0.0 published 2023-08-26; repo pushed 2023-09-28; engine last updated October 2024.

evidence.label: CI publish pipeline
evidence.detail: CI runs tests only; npm publishing is manual and no version carries provenance.
